requirement:
Parses the selector into segments in root-to-item order. An empty selector yields an empty vector. Invalid syntax returns a diagnostic.

```rust,ignore
pub fn parse_selector(selector: &str) -> Result<Vec<Segment>, SelectorError>;
```
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.outlines.parse_selector` has three obligations. The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` covers each one.

- **Empty selector gives an empty vector.** The test asserts `parse_selector("").unwrap().is_empty()`.
- **Segments come back in root-to-item order.** The test parses `impl[Thing/Trait%3CT%3E]/fn[run]#2/use@0123456789AB`. It asserts `segments[0].label` is `Named(["Thing", "Trait<T>"])`, which also checks percent-decoding. It asserts `segments[1].ordinal == Some(2)` and that `segments[1]` equals `Segment::new("fn", run).ordinal(2)`, which pins its kind, label and ordinal. It asserts `segments[2].label == Hash("0123456789ab")` and `segments[2].to_string() == "use@0123456789ab"`. Any reordering of segments would fail one of these assertions.
- **Invalid syntax returns a diagnostic.** The test loops over `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `fn[run]#0`, `use@123`, `fn[run]x` and `a//b`. Together they cover a missing bracket pair, an unclosed bracket, a missing kind, a zero ordinal, a short hash, trailing garbage and an empty segment. For each one it asserts that `parse_selector` returns an error. It also asserts that `error.selector` equals the input and that `error.message` is non-empty. Finally it asserts that `Display` includes both the input and the message.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` only checks the exported API surface. It does not test parsing behavior, and parsing behavior does not need it.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: Parses the selector into segments in root-to-item order. An empty selector yields an empty vector. Invalid syntax returns a diagnostic.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
